sectionIntro: architectural and landscape design projects, professional and academic, spanning public space, institutional design, and housing across india, nigeria, and the uk.

items.title: kotambi international cricket stadium
items.description: schematic design lead for the north stand media block, a five-level structure integrating press, commentary, camera, and broadcast facilities. concrete and glass articulated as "the eye of the stadium."
body: schematic design lead for the north stand media block of the kotambi international cricket stadium, integrating media, commentary, and broadcast facilities across a five-level structure. the brief called for a stand that could serve press, commentators, and camera crews simultaneously, without any of those functions compromising the others' sightlines.

the north stand serves as the heart of surveillance and communication for the area. dubbed "the eye" of the stadium, it houses the print media block, commentary boxes, camera controls, broadcast facilities, and the press conference room, stacked across five levels from ground level up to roughly 21 metres.

the design mirrors that watchful role: sleek lines and a strategic position give the stand optimal sightlines for media personnel and commentators, while reinforcing its symbolic significance as the vantage point overseeing everything unfolding on the field.

concrete and glass carry the narrative. concrete gives the structure its foundation of resilience and reliability, while glass brings transparency and light, connecting the enclosed media functions back to the stadium and the match beyond. sweeping roof lines and angular geometries were used to suggest movement and energy, rooting a contemporary form in the wider vocabulary of cricket architecture in india.

master plans, circulation networks, and wayfinding systems were also developed for related public, residential, and commercial projects during this period, totalling over 150,000 sq ft of built space, alongside construction documentation and contractor coordination for residential towers and apartment interiors.

items.title: gaudium school
items.description: landscape and circulation strategy for a school built around "nurturing the whole child." a designed swale doubles as water management and an interactive outdoor learning feature, using geocell instead of concrete.
body: gaudium school places a strong emphasis on holistic development and environmental sustainability, built around nurturing the whole child by fostering intellectual, emotional, physical, and social growth. the landscape and circulation strategy was developed to embody those values spatially, not just programmatically.

a shallow water body, the swale, runs through the campus doing double duty: a sustainable water management system and an engaging outdoor learning environment for students. it was designed with each contour planned to serve different functions depending on where the swale meets the built form. percolation chambers and a permeable crs stone lining facilitate natural filtration and groundwater recharge while collecting rainwater runoff.

the swale's landscape design includes dry, naturalistic plantings and rough stones, creating a visually appealing space for students to explore and observe. steps and stones let students safely access the swale when it's dry, folding it into daily use as an interactive outdoor learning feature rather than a fenced-off utility.

geocell, a material used in construction and slope protection with topsoil and other infill materials, was used in place of concrete across several landscaped areas, a more sustainable approach that avoids concrete entirely on steep slopes in narrow spaces.

large open-plan classrooms encourage interactive teaching methods, and the ample shared spaces, amphitheatre, landscaped pockets, fish pond, and sitting areas, promote social interaction and a strong sense of community throughout the school day.
